### detective-behavior-graph-definition

**Claim.** A behavior graph is a linked set of extracted and analyzed data from one or more AWS accounts; the account that enables Detective becomes the administrator account of the graph and invites or enables member accounts to contribute data.

**Write it as.** `a linked set of extracted and analyzed data` · `becomes the administrator account for a behavior graph`

**Scope.** per behavior graph.

> "When an account enables Detective, it becomes the administrator account for a behavior graph. A behavior graph is a linked set of extracted and analyzed data from one or more AWS accounts. Administrator accounts invite member accounts to contribute their data to the administrator account's behavior graph."
> — [What is Amazon Detective?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/detective/latest/userguide/what-is-detective.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### detective-faq-behavior-graph

**Claim.** Detective extracts time-based events such as logins, API calls and network traffic from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings, Security Hub findings and EKS audit logs, and builds a behavior graph of resource behavior over time.

Detective creates a behavior graph that utilizes machine learning (ML) to create a unified, interactive view of your resource behaviors and their interactions over time, specifically for these time-based events."

### detective-vs-guardduty-vs-security-hub
